subject: Charge split for mid-cycle plan change — metering + VAT question
content:
From: Elena Voronina <elena@brightbridge.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.inference <camila_reyes@redwood.inference>
Cc: Kevin O'Connor <kevin@brightbridge.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +02:00
Subject: Charge split for mid-cycle plan change — metering + VAT question

Hi Camila,

We pulled the April invoice and noticed BrightBridge was billed for both the Starter plan and Scale plan for the same billing window (Apr 1–5). I attached the invoice and our local usage CSV — it looks like some of the tokens were counted twice: the Starter charge line and the Scale overage line both reference similar token volumes.

Two quick facts that might matter: we upgraded from Starter to Scale on Apr 1 at ~10:15 UTC, and we have two active API keys (one for prod, one for dev) — both point to the same project. Can you confirm how Redwood attributes usage during upgrades? Also, our finance team needs to know whether this is taxable: BrightBridge is Estonia-registered (VAT ID: EE123456789), so if reverse-charge applies we need the corrected invoice.

Attachments: 2027-04-invoice-BB-8943.pdf (invoice), usage-export-20270401-20270405.csv (our export), vat-receipt-uk.pdf (our VAT memo)

Can you investigate and let us know the next steps? Ideally we get a corrected invoice or credit before our month-end close.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Infrastructure
BrightBridge AI
elena@brightbridge.ai

----
From: camila_reyes@redwood.inference <camila_reyes@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Voronina <elena@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.inference, marcus_lin@redwood.inference
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:03:21 -07:00
Subject: Re: Charge split for mid-cycle plan change — metering + VAT question

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear notes and the attachments. I'm looping in Naomi from Billing and Marcus on the infra-side so we can lookup the raw metering and the relevant model-tokenization details.

A few clarifying Qs while we start the investigation:
- Did you switch the plan via the Console UI or via the API? (Console changes follow a single upgrade path; API subscription creates a new allocation in some cases.)
- Can you confirm which API key the production traffic used between 10:00–11:00 UTC on Apr 1? The usage CSV you sent has two keys listed and we want to make sure we're attributing correctly.

Prelim timeline: we'll aim to get a full usage export + reconciliation notes within 48 hours and propose any credit/proration if there was an overlap. Naomi — would you prefer to issue a provisional credit or wait for Marcus's tokenization analysis?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.inference

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.inference <naomi_feldman@redwood.inference>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.inference, marcus_lin@redwood.inference
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 10:45:33 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Preliminary billing reconciliation for BB-8943

Camila / Marcus — quick internal summary after pulling the first-pass exports:
- What happened: The upgrade on Apr 1 triggered allocation of a new subscription object; for ~35 minutes both Starter and Scale were active for the same account ID while the old allocation was still draining. That created overlapping metering windows in the billing engine, which is why two separate lines appear on the invoice.
- Token delta: Marcus, can you confirm, but sampled traffic shows an effective +12% token count on our side compared to BrightBridge's CSV. We believe the difference is due to the recent tokenizer alias (model alias v2.1) rollout two weeks ago — it tokenizes a handful of common punctuation-heavy payloads differently.
- VAT: Since BrightBridge provided an EU VAT ID, reverse-charge should apply (no VAT charged on the corrected invoice). We'll still issue a corrected invoice with the VAT ID listed.

Proposed remediation options:
1) Issue a one-time pro-rated credit for the Starter allocation for the overlapping window (we'd credit the Starter line and adjust the invoice). Estimated: $3,250 credit.
2) Do not change past metering but provide an on-account credit equivalent to the tokenization delta (roughly $2,750) in addition to correcting the overlap.

My preference is option 1 (clean corrected invoice + transparency). I'd like approval to proceed and to include a short note explaining the tokenizer change as context.

Attachments (internal): billing-worksheet-20270403.xlsx

Naomi Feldman
Head of Billing, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.inference

----
From: marcus_lin@redwood.inference <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.inference, camila_reyes@redwood.inference
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 14:22:11 -07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Preliminary billing reconciliation for BB-8943

Confirming the technical root cause here. Sampling and token diff: I pulled 500 requests from the customer's prod key and re-run tokenization under the legacy tokenizer (alias v2.0) and the new alias (v2.1). Result: median token count increased ~12% for these payloads, with worst-case ~18% on punctuation-heavy strings.

Notes:
- The metering engine is correct to have logged both allocations while they were active; the overlap was a side-effect of the upgrade path we still support (create+drain).
- Retroactively changing the metering algorithm is risky (audit trail) — we should not re-score old requests. Instead I support issuing the credit for the overlapping allocation and, optionally, an adjustment to account for the tokenization delta as a customer goodwill concession.

Example of command I ran (for internal audit):
> python scripts/token_compare.py --input sample-requests.json --alias-old v2.0 --alias-new v2.1 --output token-diff-summary.csv

I'll attach the token-diff-summary.csv to the internal record.

—Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.inference

----
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Voronina <elena@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.inference>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 15:03:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Charge split for mid-cycle plan change — metering + VAT question

Hi Elena — thanks for your patience while we investigated. Summary and next steps: 

1) Cause: the platform created a new subscription allocation when the upgrade occurred and the previous allocation drained for ~35 minutes. That produced two billable lines for the same traffic window. Separately, a tokenizer alias roll-out (v2.1) increased token counts for some payloads which explains the token-count delta between our export and yours.

2) Remedy: we will issue a corrected invoice that removes the Starter allocation for the overlapping 35-minute window and apply a one-time credit of $3,250 (line item: "overlap proration credit"). We will NOT re-score historical requests; the credit is how we reconcile the overcount + customer impact.

3) VAT: we will reissue the corrected invoice with BrightBridge's EU VAT ID (EE123456789) and mark it as reverse-charge (no VAT collected). Please confirm the VAT ID you provided is final.

4) Timing: corrected invoice + credit should be posted by EOD Apr 6 and will show up as a negative line on your invoice. Naomi will send the official credit memo and updated invoice PDF.

If that works for you we'll proceed; otherwise let me know if you'd prefer the alternative (smaller credit + token-delta concession) and we can discuss.

Thanks again,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.inference
